newsitem.title: FRANCE: French agents in "fruitless" talks with Air France.
newsitem.headline: French agents in "fruitless" talks with Air France.

text.p: France's air freight forwarding association (SNAGFA) said a meeting with Air France Cargo officials over a fuel surcharge applied at the beginning of the month had been "fruitless".
Air France gave no indication it would go back on its decision and both parties left the meeting agreeing to disagree, SNAGFA general secretary, Bruno Charrois, told Reuters.

"We put our point across in stressing that if Air France persisted in its approach we would consider appealing to France's Commission de la Concurrence (Fair Trade Commission) to establish whether the airline was in contravention of commercial law given that the surcharges could be interpreted as price collusion with other airlines, an argument which it Air France dismissed, Charrols stated."
SNAGFA would continue to adopt a "wait and see" attitude leaving the door open for fresh negotiations with Air France Cargo.

"What agents found deeply disturbing about the surcharges was firstly the very short notice given of their application and then their simulataneous implementation. Air France just don't seem to understand our position and the whole issue has left a bitter taste," Charrois added.
Meanwhile, another French carrier, Air Outre Mer (AOM), said it would be applying a 50 centimes/kilo fuel surcharge on freight rates from November 15.

"It's always been our policy to give customers reasonable prior notice of rates increases. Notification only a few days before the increases are to be implemented is just not our way of doing business," an AOM cargo official told Reuters.
Fellow French airline, Air Liberte, said it had not yet taken a decision on implementing a fuel surcharge. -- Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
